curry_chef.text: {greeting} Leeds and Bradford do a cracking curry. Families came from Pakistan, India and Bangladesh to work in the mills in the 1950s and 60s, and brought the cooking with them.
Now a curry's as Yorkshire as a pudding. Some say Bradford's the curry capital of Britain. Don't say that too loud in Leeds.

then.text: Dal, rice, a frozen bag of spinach. That's dinner, and it's cheap.

else.text: People think eating well costs a fortune. A big pot of dal costs pence a portion: red lentils, an onion, a tin of tomatoes, some spice, and rice on the side.
Cook once, eat three times. Freeze the rest. Frozen veg is as good as fresh, and it never goes soft in the drawer.

then.text: Not quite. That's 36p per 100g. Check the unit price on the shelf label and compare.
Yes. That's 28p per 100g against 36p. The bigger pack isn't always cheaper, so check the unit price every time.
The marketing people love you. The unit price on the shelf label (per 100g or per kilo) is where the truth lives.

else.text: Plan the week before you shop, and shop with a list. Look at the reduced shelf near closing time. Leftovers are tomorrow's lunch, not a failure.
Skip the fancy spice jars until you know what you use. A big bag from the corner shop costs a fraction of the price.
Take a pie for the road. Not mine, mine's the dal. Nobody argues with a pork pie.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
